# reac-repacer / fuzz_lock

reac-repacer's own fuzz target `fuzz_lock` ([source](source/fuzz_lock.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over reac-repacer 0.2.3 (FreeREAC/reac-repacer at 3ac1cf10).

Takes a rate selector byte, a name-length byte (its value modulo 16), an interface name of that many bytes (an empty name, or one holding a NUL, space, tab, CR or LF, is rejected), and then the text of a warm-start lock file. It asks the lock reader for the saved frame period of that interface at that rate, checks that the answer is the same when the byte after the text is "0" and when it is a space, and compares it with the period the harness finds itself by parsing the record grammar (port, period, rate label, within 5% of the standard period, last record wins, at most 65536 bytes).

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Linked against a static library of src/repace_wire.c and src/repace_conf.c, and one of libreac's src/reac.c, the files reac-repacer's own libFuzzer build compiles; built as a static riscv64 program for the standard driver in place of libFuzzer.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- The answer depends only on the text's bytes: the same text followed by "0" and followed by a space gives the same period ([lines 120-141](source/fuzz_lock.c#L120-L141)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The period restored is the one the lock grammar gives, as parsed independently by the harness ([lines 143-179](source/fuzz_lock.c#L143-L179)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch reac-repacer` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |

| asan | `fuzz_lock.asan` | 561,768 | `ebbd035f6e8d0bc4269207f57043129cb8e6108c3887da8d5ed4389978de5e5d` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
